utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC
utterances.text: I don't know, but I do know that the director of that organisation insisted that they move out of that building. Later, that was Piric Lafet [phoen], who ended up also in Zasavica and went through all the suffering that I had been inflicted also.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: You've never entered Cafe AS?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC
utterances.text: No, never.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us, Mr. Jasarevic: As you've said that you've seen members of the 4th Detachment standing in and around the Cafe AS, did you see also other people? As you're a person from Samac, you must have known many people of Samac. Did you see Omer Nalic, your brother-in-law?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did see him. I did see him. He went into the gambling establishment there, together with your lawyer, Pisarevic. They were gambling there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Did you see Alija Fitozovic entering there?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC
utterances.text: Alija would be a patron of all cafes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: What about Salkic, and others?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC
utterances.text: No, I didn't see them.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Now, let us return to this flag. Did you see that flag of this Yugoslav flag in front of Mladost? Did you see it between January and to the moment that the headquarters moved to AS?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC
utterances.text: I didn't follow the event.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: When did you, for the first time, see that Yugoslav flag hanging out there?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC
utterances.text: It was unusual -- it wasn't unusual to see that Yugoslav flag. For each and every holiday it was hanging there. But I know that headquarters of the 4th Detachment were in Mladost.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Let me ask about another subject. You were answering to the question of the Prosecutor concerning the incident in Cafe Molla.

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC
utterances.text: I don't know about Cafe Molla.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: I apologise. Cafe Valentino, when those boys were killed there.

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember: You said that you spoke to the owner of the cafe immediately after that event.

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And that he told you that they were playing with a hand grenade and that this hand grenade was activated while they were playing with it.

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes. It wasn't the first time that such events occurred, that they would be playing with a hand grenade.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: This was an accident?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it was an accident.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: I mixed the two cafe, Molla and Cafe Valentino. Ratif Atic was the owner of Cafe Molla?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I know him.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And you know that members of the SDA were meeting there?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: You have also mentioned here an incident which happened with the members of the 4th Detachment, when Tota and Danilo were injured. Do you remember that event?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: That happened in front of Cafe Molla?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC
utterances.text: No. It happened at the corner, at the very entrance of the cafe, at the very corner of the market, towards the main street. There I saw the Lada, which was riddled with bullets.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Does Molla -- is Molla nearby?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: A bit diagonally across the street?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Diagonally some 50 metres across the street.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: You have mentioned that you were passing by Cafe AS, that you were seeing these people. Can you tell me: Did you see them when you were going to work or when you were returning?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC
utterances.text: When I was returning from work, but I also saw them when I went to work. They were there on duty. I saw Stojanka's son. I saw them going out of Cafe AS in the morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know that Cafe AS was open practically throughout the day and night before these events?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC
utterances.text: No, I did not know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Jasarevic, in your statement, and also during your testimony today, you had mentioned that on that morning of the 17th of April, you were -- you got ready a bit earlier, around 5.00 a.m., to go to work. That is paragraph 35?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Ms. Reidy?

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Yes. It's just -- if the Defence counsel could please refer to the paragraph, if they say it's in the statement as well, for the benefit, I believe, of the Bench, as well as for us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: For example, the last paragraph he mentioned when he talked about the incident between the 4th Detachment, you know, Defence counsel had put in his own words about the persons who were injured. It's not in the statement. Until you find the statement, you don't see that. I'm not objecting to that. I think that whole incident has been more than enough discussed before, but if in the future Defence counsel could adopt the habit of telling us which paragraph, it would be more than useful.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. I'm sure Mr. Krgovic will follow that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: So we're referring to paragraph 35. And you said that at about 5.00 a.m. You were getting ready for work.

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Everybody morning I would be getting up at 5.00 a.m. and in my statement, I also said why I got up so early to go to work.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: When did your shift begin?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC
utterances.text: At 6.00 a.m., and I always walked to my job.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And that morning you normally went to work?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC
utterances.text: When everything calmed down, I tried to, by phone, to check whether everything was all right, we'd be working, and in my statement I also said why I went so early to work and why I had to be there first.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Jasarevic, you try and answer all my questions, because in your statement, this has already been written down. This was an introduction, and wait for my question which I will raise. I wanted to ask you: When did you leave your home that morning?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC
utterances.text: Before 5.30 a.m.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And you went to the health centre?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC
utterances.text: No. I passed by the health centre.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: You didn't arrive to your place of work; you stopped at a certain point and you returned home?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC
utterances.text: It's stated in my statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: How long did you stay outside your home?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC
utterances.text: Somebody from the dark said, "Why are you here? Do you want to lose your head?" I immediately returned to my apartment.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: I'm asking -- I don't know how distant is the health centre from your home. So you must have returned after half an hour, 40 minutes, or less.

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC
utterances.text: Five, ten minutes, at the most.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: That morning when you were returning, did you see any military vehicles along the streets you were moving?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: You didn't see any people moving by these vehicles, or hiding?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN JASAREVIC
utterances.text: I saw them -- I saw that in the afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, it's practically time to end our session today, because I'd be passing on to another subject, so I propose that we adjourn and resume tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Very well. Yes, Mr. Pantelic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Since we have a couple of minutes to the adjournment, to the break, maybe I can address the Chamber. Well, I was informed by my client, as well as the other defendants, that based on the information that they have in Detention Unit - obviously they are speaking with the other defendants in the other cases - that there is certain, well, need or habit to, from time to time, by the end of the day -- maybe the defendants could address the Trial Chamber with certain issues or -- I don't know. Personally, I am not familiar with the practice of the other Trial Chambers. I even didn't have enough time to explore this matter. But maybe our defendants can clarify that in details, what is the reason to address the Trial Chamber and what could be the topic. Yes, and I think the witness could be released, because these are the procedural matters.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Maybe we can clear the witness. Witness, the proceedings will continue tomorrow at 9.00. Yes. Is there anything that the any of the defendants wanted to say to the Trial Chamber?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED TADIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I turned on the microphone when the cross-examination began. I wanted to object the fact that we have been given a very short period of time in order to prepare with the cross-examination. Some new facts emerged, and we didn't have enough time, so the questions are not the best possible questions. This is what I wanted to object at the time. I don't have anything particularly to say now, but I think it would be useful if occasionally we would be given a right to address you. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Blagoje Simic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED SIMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I initiated this idea of allowing us occasionally to address you at the end of the day. I have several objections to make, and one of the main ones is the identification of myself by witnesses. I claim that I don't know most of these witnesses --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Let me say this to all the defendants: Matters relating to procedure or the way the case is going should be left to the Defence counsel. The Defence counsel should be able to raise such matters. The matters you may raise with the Chamber are those to do with perhaps your health or whatever is happening to you in the Detention Unit. Otherwise, matters of procedure should be left to the Defence counsel. That's why they're here.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: If Your Honours please, there's an added danger as well that I can see looming here. Dr. Blagoje Simic, I gather, was just about to launch into or say something about an issue that is purely an evidentiary issue. The more he says, the more I will cross-examine about what he -- when my time comes, of course. And what's the situation -- what sort of situation is going to develop here? We don't know that these witnesses are going to give evidence. Is the situation going to develop where they stand up and make statements and I don't have a right to cross-examine?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: I don't think, Mr. Di Fazio, you should worry about that --

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: No. Well, I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: -- because the procedure of the Chamber is quite clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Because those incidences before the Trial Chambers are matters best left to those Trial Chambers.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I'm not talking about what happens elsewhere, but just for the sake of the defendants, so they understand that it's not just a question of standing up. There are all sorts of implications that follow, and so on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: So I would -- I mean, it's not for me to advise them, of course, and I don't, but I say that from the Prosecution's point of view, the safest thing is do things through your lawyers rather than yourself. And that's my view. But in any event, let me say this, and so that Defence counsel understand: that if matters were ever to be uttered by defendants in Court, then I would, of course, only be happy if that were to be covered by my right to cross-examine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Very well. We shall adjourn and continue tomorrow morning. This does not mean that the defendants cannot address the Court, but I did indicate on what matters the defendants can address the Court directly. Otherwise, it should always be through their Defence counsel. We will continue the proceedings tomorrow at 0900 hours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 4th day of July, 2002, at 9.00 a.m.
